basic_info: Mason, adult, referred by primary care doctor for kidney stones
present_illness: Sudden right back pain radiating to groin one week ago, CT scan confirmed kidney stone, straining urine without visible stones. Patient described intense pain in the right back radiating to the groin, accompanied by sweating and nausea, but no vomiting or hematuria. No pain or burning when urinating, and no feeling of incomplete bladder emptying. Patient was prescribed oxycodone for pain and continues to take Tylenol for breakthrough pain. Patient reports pain has been mostly gone since the initial episode, with occasional brief recurrences. Patient has been increasing water intake to help pass the stone and does not track dietary intake closely, though he does not consume a lot of salt or protein.
past_history: No prior history of kidney stones reported. No relevant surgical history. No known allergies. No family history of kidney stones or urological conditions.
aux_exam: CT scan performed (date not specified, stone size: approximately 0.5 cm, location: right ureter). Blood work and urinalysis ordered but results not yet received. Urine color is slightly darker than usual but no other changes noted.
